themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, up 2300% from a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69), suggesting a sudden emergence of unlicensed or problematic street food operations in Sunset Park.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme spike
First reported surge of this type in recent complaint data
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed vendors clustering in specific neighborhoods or transit hubs? Interview Department of Health enforcement.
What changed this week to trigger such a dramatic spike—new vendor recruitment, reduced enforcement, or seasonal shift?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 36 THIS WEEK, up 206% from an 11.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.96), indicating a sharp uptick in restaurant, bar, or construction-related disturbances.
evidence: 36 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.96 indicates statistically significant deviation
Complements existing high baseline of noise complaints (648 residential noise complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Map the 36 complaints: are they concentrated in a specific commercial corridor (e.g., Fifth Avenue, Fourth Avenue)? Is a new venue or event triggering this?
Interview residents and business owners about what type of noise—nightlife, construction, delivery trucks—and whether enforcement has been responsive.

themes_detail.label: General 311 Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: General/miscellaneous 311 complaints spiked to 19 THIS WEEK, up 271% from a 5.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.3), suggesting a broad-based uptick in resident complaints across multiple unreported categories.
evidence: 19 general complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.3 indicates statistically extreme spike
Nature of 'general' complaints unclear—could indicate residents filing catch-all tickets when specific categories don't fit
reporting_angles: Request detailed 311 complaint narratives from this week's general category to identify what underlying issues residents are reporting.
Is the spike tied to a specific incident, event, or service failure that residents are flagging through multiple channels?

themes_detail.label: Appliance Failure Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Appliance complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, up 167% from a 2.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.94), potentially signaling a pattern of failing building infrastructure or tenant disputes over landlord repair responsibilities.
evidence: 7 appliance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.94 indicates statistically significant spike
Complements existing HEAT/HOT WATER complaints (749 over 90 days), suggesting broader building maintenance failures
reporting_angles: Interview HPD about complaint patterns: are specific buildings or landlords repeat offenders? Is this a winter-season spike tied to heating systems?
Survey tenants in buildings with recent appliance complaints: are landlords delaying repairs, or is this a supply chain/contractor availability issue?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Complaints (Lagged Signal)
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints peaked at 5 three weeks ago (900% above the 0.5 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks, z-score: 9.0), but the signal is now 3 weeks old and requires verification of current status before committing reporting resources.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.0 indicates most extreme spike in dataset (highest severity)
No recent follow-up data available; unclear if this was a one-time spike or sustained issue
reporting_angles: Check NYPD precinct data for the past 3 weeks: have drug-related arrests or complaints remained elevated, or was it a one-week spike?
Interview 77th Precinct and community organizations: what geographic area was affected, and what enforcement response occurred?
